trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is the list's finishing line: it pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, with nothing extra to do. Everything on the list is single-player — no online, DLC or difficulty trophies — and the published guides put the full run at roughly 200 hours, most of it inside the 100% checklist behind A Long Road. Plan one long playthrough, keep rotating manual saves, and treat this trophy as a progress report rather than a task. Tip: if it does not pop when you expect, compare your earned list against the checklist here; the missing item is almost always a cleanup trophy from the middle stages of the roadmap.
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies on the list
Let the platinum pop automatically
If it stalls, audit the list for one missed cleanup trophy

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: This pops automatically at the end of Gone Fishing, the opening mission of Chapter 1, so it cannot be missed. Treat the mission as the game's tutorial stretch: movement, driving and the basics of the first protagonist's life. There is no performance requirement — no medal, timer or optional objective is attached. Tip: start your save discipline here and keep a manual save at the start of Chapter 1, because the game has no mission replay.
steps: Start the story and play Chapter 1
Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing
Make a manual save at the chapter boundary

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing Chapter 1; the published guides note it registers as you move into Chapter 2's opening mission. It is a pure progression trophy with no optional conditions, so a normal story run earns it. Optional missions you finish during the chapter still count toward the 100% checklist even before that checklist becomes visible. Tip: before closing the chapter, do Lucia's balcony meditation at Jason's house (see Positive Mental Attitude) — it is the one interaction the guides flag as potentially missable.
steps: Play through Chapter 1's main missions
Do the Chapter 1 balcony meditation before finishing
Cross into Chapter 2 to bank the trophy

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Completing Chapter 2 earns this; the guides note it registers during Chapter 3's opening stretch. Chapter 2 is also where both protagonists become playable together, which unlocks the partner trophies and, later, the final meditation spot. Nothing in the chapter is missable for trophy purposes. Tip: from here on, scan every new vehicle with the WAiNK app as you encounter it, so Whip It Good builds up naturally instead of becoming a late-game hunt.
steps: Complete Chapter 2's main missions
Start Chapter 3 to trigger the unlock
Begin scanning new vehicles with the WAiNK app

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3. The Cartel Heist sits inside this chapter and carries its own trophy (Break the Bank), so the chapter pays out twice. Progression is all that is required — no optional objectives or medals gate it. Keep doing optional missions as they appear: you need 100 of them across the game for the 100% checklist, and there are far more available than that. Tip: keep a manual save at the chapter's start and end and rotate the spare slots.
steps: Complete Chapter 3's main missions, including The Cartel Heist
Move into Chapter 4 to bank the trophy
Keep a manual save at the chapter boundary

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4, the busiest chapter for named-mission trophies: Child's Play, Headliners and VCIA Takedown all live here. An optional Chapter 4 mission also opens up the bank vaults used by Maximum Withdrawal, so unlock them now rather than during cleanup. Everything in the chapter remains reachable afterwards in free roam. Tip: with the finale approaching, park one manual save at the chapter's end and do not overwrite it.
steps: Complete Chapter 4's main missions
Take the optional mission that opens the bank vaults
Save at the chapter boundary

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold for finishing the final story mission. Once it is done the game returns you to free roam, so nothing after this point is locked away — the entire cleanup happens post-credits. There is no difficulty setting to worry about and no medal requirement on the mission itself. Tip: save before the finale in its own slot; with no mission replay, that save is your only way back to the ending stretch.
steps: Reach the final story mission
Complete it to roll the credits
Continue in free roam for the cleanup stages

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run, which the guides place in Chapter 2. It is a mandatory mission on the story path, so the trophy is automatic and cannot be missed. No optional objectives or performance targets apply. Tip: story missions also move several background counters (discoveries, optional content), so there is no reason to rush past the areas it takes you through.
steps: Reach the Breakfast Run mission in Chapter 2
Complete the mission

sources.name: PowerPyx — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap · Trust

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a set-piece story mission in Chapter 3; finishing it earns the trophy with no side conditions. It doubles as training for the free-roam robbery trophies: vault work, escapes and wanted-level management all return in Maximum Withdrawal and A Classic Blitz Play. Tip: pay attention to how the heist handles its escape phase — losing the heat quickly and switching vehicles is the same skill the silver robbery trophy grades you on.
steps: Reach The Cartel Heist in Chapter 3
Complete the heist and its escape

sources.name: PowerPyx — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap · Break the Bank

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete Child's Play, a main mission the guides place in Chapter 4. Like the other named-mission trophies it is awarded for completion alone — no score, time or optional objective is attached. It sits in the chapter alongside Headliners and VCIA Takedown, so Chapter 4 banks several bronzes in a row. Tip: none; play it as it comes and keep your chapter-boundary saves current.
steps: Reach Child's Play in Chapter 4
Complete the mission

sources.name: PowerPyx — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap · Family Matters

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete Headliners, another of Chapter 4's named main missions. Completion is the whole requirement; the trophy cannot be missed because the mission is compulsory story progress. Tip: if you are chaining Chapter 4's missions, this is a good moment to also unlock the bank vaults via the chapter's optional mission, while you are already in the area.
steps: Reach Headliners in Chapter 4
Complete the mission

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete VCIA Takedown, a Chapter 4 main mission set around VCIA, Vice City's international airport. The trophy is for completion only and is unmissable. Remember the location: the airport is also where the free-roam trophy Catch Me If You Can is earned later. Tip: while the mission has you at the airport, note the layout of the field and hangars for that return visit.
steps: Reach VCIA Takedown in Chapter 4
Complete the mission

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory, which the guides place in Chapter 5, the final chapter. It is the last of the named-mission bronzes and, like the rest, is awarded for completion alone on the compulsory story path. After it, only the finale stands between you and the gold for the final mission. Tip: keep a fresh manual save before pushing into the endgame sequence.
steps: Reach Operation Savage Glory in Chapter 5
Complete the mission

sources.name: PowerPyx — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap · Snow Storm

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The long gold. After the story, a 100% Completion checklist appears under Progress > Stats, and filling it earns this trophy — but '100%' is generous: the guides put it near 60% true completion, with most side quests and many collectible types not required at all. The demanding parts are the categories required in full — robberies, underwater discoveries, shooting ranges, drone races and Bret's quests — plus 70 of the 80 challenges and any 100 optional missions. Progress made during the story already counts, and nothing on the checklist is missable. Tip: work the checklist screen itself as your to-do list after the credits, and leave the hardest challenges for last, since you are allowed to skip ten.
steps: Finish the story to reveal the checklist
Open Progress > Stats > 100% Completion
Clear the fully-required categories first: robberies, ranges, drone races, Bret's quests
Reach 70 of 80 challenges and 100 optional missions
Top off the partial categories until the checklist reads 100%

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete any 250 of the game's 397 stunt events. They fall into four families — 130 stunt jumps, 202 flights under bridges, 40 knife flights between buildings and 25 base jumps — and any mix counts toward the 250. The under-bridge flights are widely reported as the quickest to bank. Progress is tracked per region under Progress > Activities > Stunts, and completed stunts stay marked on the map's Exploration filter. Tip: the 100% checklist wants 300 stunts, so keep going past 250 while you are in a stunt mood.
steps: Open the map's Exploration filter to list stunt spots
Start with under-bridge flights for quick completions
Mix in jumps, knife flights and base jumps
Reach 250 completed stunts

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every kind of activity once. The trophy tracker counts nine activity types, and you can watch them under Touch Pad > Progress > Activities, where each type shows how many times you have done it. The story introduces most types on its own; the rest appear as blue icons once the map is unfogged. In practice this pops by itself during a full playthrough. Tip: late in the run, open the Activities page and look for any type still showing zero — that is your only homework.
steps: Open Progress > Activities to see the nine types
Try each type at least once
Use the map's Activities filter to find any missing type

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal every Shooting Range challenge: 42 golds spread across 12 ranges, as the published lists and this bounty's own rules text both state. A gold is a score target rather than a win against an opponent, so learn each challenge's target pattern and retry until the medal lands; ranges stay available for the whole game. All 42 are also required in full by the 100% checklist, which makes this one of the list's true long poles. Tip: settle on one comfortable weapon per range and run its challenges back-to-back while the layouts are fresh in your mind.
steps: Visit each of the 12 shooting ranges
Learn each challenge's scoring targets
Retry until every challenge shows a gold medal — 42 in total

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations. Only one win per location is needed for the trophy, even though the locations host 42 races in total and the 100% checklist wants all of them — so fly the shortest event at each spot and move on. Drone races are handling tests: a clean line through the gates beats raw speed. Tip: if a location's win is elusive, learn the gate order at cruising pace first, then push for pace on the next run.
steps: Find a Top Fun drone race location
Win one race there
Repeat at all 14 locations

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — winning the same race twice does not count. There are about 40 races in the game, so you can take the half that suits you and skip the rest. Wins count across race types, so mix road, off-road and water events as they appear on the map. Tip: keep track of which races you have already won; the map marks discovered races, and variety matters more than volume here.
steps: Enter races as they appear on the map
Win each race once
Reach 20 distinct race wins

Tip: learn the basic fishing loop on ordinary spots first (which also feeds Master of None), so Cal's challenge is the only new thing you are dealing with.

Start a game

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots, spread across 10 locations; most are ordinary free-roam visits, and doing a spot with both protagonists also feeds the 100% checklist (which itself only asks for 15 of the 18). The catch is the first one: in Chapter 1, after the mission Down to Earth, Lucia announces a morning meditation at Jason's house and heads to the balcony — follow her and accept. That interaction disappears when Chapter 1 ends, and PowerPyx and GTABase both flag this as the list's only potentially missable trophy point; whether the trophy strictly needs it is unconfirmed, but the safe play costs two minutes. Tip: keep a Chapter 1 save untouched until the balcony meditation is done.

Follow her to the balcony and accept the meditation
Visit the remaining meditation spots across Leonida — 18 in total
Do the final spot once both protagonists are playable together

trophies.missableNote: Potential missable — flagged as the safe default. The window: in Chapter 1, after Down to Earth, Lucia’s morning meditation on the balcony at Jason’s house becomes unavailable once Chapter 1 ends. The decision rule: if that balcony meditation is one of the 18 marked spots, the trophy is missable; if it is not, the trophy stays earnable in free roam. Published sources do not resolve which is true, so the flag stays on and the two-minute meditation is worth doing. Either way, the 100% checklist needs only 15 of the 18 spots, so A Long Road (100% completion) is never at risk.

Tip: when Bret's hunt is active, treat it like a strand finale: prepare first, travel to the hunting ground, and finish the unique animal rather than wandering off mid-quest.

Tip: the map's Exploration filter lists discovered spots by name, which makes hunting down the last few far easier than driving around hoping to spot them.

Clear the easiest categories first

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — one per gang, nine gangs in the list data. Gang operations are marked criminal sites on the map; you do not need to clear them all, just hit every gang once. These robberies also feed the robbery category of the 100% checklist, which is required in full. Tip: keep a simple tally by gang name — the last unrobbed gang is usually the one whose territory you rarely visit.

Rob one operation per gang
Cover all 9 gangs

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is one of the list's one-off world moments: a specific leisure interaction at the Ocean Beach area rather than a mission or a counter. Look for the interaction prompt at a beachfront spot with the view the description promises, and take the drink. Tip: go in free roam at a relaxed moment — no wanted level, no mission active — and work along the beachfront bars of Ocean Beach.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom 'in classic style' — drive a car out through the showroom glass. Vehicle showrooms are Vice City's car dealerships: get into a display car (or bring your own inside) and exit through the windows rather than the door. The published guides pin this to a specific showroom moment with screenshots. Tip: pick a showroom with big street-facing glass and a car already on the floor.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Do the 'follow-through' at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — a bowling action at that specific alley ('follow-through' is the bowler's arm motion after releasing the ball). Bowling is also one of the nine activity types, so a proper game here covers ground for Master of None as well. Play a real game at the Kolt alley rather than looking for a shortcut. Tip: combine the visit with Ten Pin, the list's other bowling pun, if you can engineer its melee drive-by nearby.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Another of the list's deliberately vague one-offs: 'a partnership with mass appeal'. Read together with the partner trophies, it points at a Jason-and-Lucia moment performed in public — the kind of thing the game's social layer celebrates. The cited guides had not pinned down the exact trigger at the time of writing, so treat this as an exploration trophy: try partner activities in busy public places once both protagonists are playable together. Tip: if it pops unexpectedly, note what you were doing — this is one of the trophies the community is still documenting. Sources checked — PowerPyx, GTABase, KeenGamer and GTA-Zone: none of them documents a confirmed, tested trigger for this trophy, so follow the official description.

Do partner activities in busy public places

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: PlayStation tracks this as a counter that runs to 500 — the game's dialogue and interaction choices. In other words it is cumulative: choices made across story conversations and world interactions add up, and the trophy lands when the counter completes. Despite the ominous description ('for better or worse'), no cited guide flags it as missable or branch-locking; the separate 'Irredeemable' criminal profile is permanent, but the guides confirm it does not affect trophies. Tip: talk to people and take optional interactions as you go instead of skipping conversations, and the counter fills itself.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' — the natural reading is: fail at something, then succeed at the same thing on the retry. The cited guides had not confirmed the exact activity at the time of writing, which makes this an experiment trophy: when a challenge, race or activity attempt fails, retry it immediately and win. Tip: keep a mental note the first time you retry-and-win anything; if the trophy does not pop, move to the next activity type and repeat the pattern there. Sources checked — PowerPyx, GTABase, KeenGamer and GTA-Zone: none of them documents a confirmed, tested trigger for this trophy, so follow the official description.

Succeed on the second try

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: A hidden oddity trophy: 'What the hell just happened?' Guide sites list its unlock method as unconfirmed; the name is an X-Files nod, and it belongs to the list's UFO-and-strangeness corner, so it is expected to pop when you witness a specific strange event in the world. Until the community pins it down, the honest strategy is exploration: investigate odd sightings, especially at night and in the remote corners of Leonida. Tip: this is a cleanup-stage trophy — do not stall your run hunting it early. Sources checked — PowerPyx, GTABase, KeenGamer and GTA-Zone: none of them documents a confirmed, tested trigger for this trophy, so follow the official description.

Investigate strange sightings or events
Witness the event fully when you find it

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock a person down by striking them with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — the 'melee drive-by'; the bowling name is a pun on knocking down a pin. Ride or drive past a pedestrian and swing a melee weapon so the hit lands while you are still moving. Guide sites note the precise method was still being confirmed at the time of writing. Tip: a motorcycle at moderate speed gives you the reach and control for this; pick a lone pedestrian and swing early. Sources checked — PowerPyx, GTABase, KeenGamer and GTA-Zone: none of them documents a confirmed, tested trigger for this trophy, so follow the official description.
steps: Take a melee weapon and a vehicle — a bike works best
Ride past a pedestrian at moderate speed
Land a melee hit while moving

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies; your fences and contacts wash them into clean money, and it is the cumulative laundered total that counts. This pairs naturally with the robbery trophies — every vault, truck and gang operation feeds it. Tip: never sit on marked bills; launder after every job so the counter keeps moving while you work on other stages.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops, counted cumulatively. Clothing, vehicles, weapons and services all feed the one total, so an ordinary geared-up playthrough gets most of the way there on its own. It is effectively unmissable on a platinum run. Tip: if you are short late in the game, vehicle purchases and garage properties (see Little Boxes) burn money fastest.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all eight garage properties. Garages are purchasable properties across Leonida, and each needs its price ready, which makes this a mid-to-late-game trophy once robbery income is flowing. Owning them also gives your vehicle collection homes, which supports the discovery and registration trophies. Tip: buy garages as new areas open up rather than saving for a single spree — the map coverage helps everything else on the list.

trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. When you acquire a vehicle you want to keep, register it through the app so it becomes yours; ten registrations complete the trophy. It pairs with Whip It Good: scan broadly for discoveries, then register the keepers. Tip: register vehicles you actually use — your personal vehicles double as the fastest travel options for the cleanup stages.

roadmap.title: Roadmap to the Platinum — Vice Got a Price!
roadmap.intro: One playthrough, no difficulty settings and no online trophies: the published guides put the platinum at roughly 200 hours and a 4/10 difficulty. There is no mission replay, but free roam continues after the story, so almost everything can be cleaned up post-credits. Keep a manual save at the start and end of every chapter (the game offers 15 manual slots) and never use cheats on a trophy run — they disable trophies and saving.

stages.name: Play the story — chapters and named missions
stages.rationale: The five chapters (about 60–80 hours) award every story trophy automatically on completion, in list order from Gone Fishing to the final mission. Do the Chapter 1 balcony meditation during this stage (see the missables note), take optional missions as they appear, and scan vehicles and study animals as you travel — all of it counts toward later stages.
stages.warning: Chapter 1 expiry: Lucia’s balcony meditation at Jason’s house (Positive Mental Attitude) becomes unavailable the moment Chapter 1 ends — do it before you finish the chapter.

stages.name: Stranger strands and character quest lines
stages.rationale: Finish the named characters' final missions — Andy (Lucia), Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone (Jason) — and Bret's hunting line, and complete eight qualifying stranger strands for the Strangers & Freaks silver. Trophy quest givers all return after the story, so nothing here can be locked out.

stages.name: Collectibles and exploration
stages.rationale: The map-wide counters: all 18 meditation spots, 3 full card sets, 100 WAiNK locations, 100 discovered vehicles and every area of Leonida explored. These reward steady habits during the story more than a dedicated grind at the end.

stages.name: Activities, ranges and challenges
stages.rationale: 250 stunts, one try of each of the nine activity types, all 42 shooting-range golds, a drone-race win at all 14 locations, 20 race wins, Cal's fishing challenge, one arcade game and 50 challenges. The shooting ranges and drone races are required in full by the 100% checklist, so this stage is on the critical path.

stages.name: Free-roam feats and robberies
stages.rationale: The one-off moments and the robbery set: partner feats, five bank vaults, an armored truck, one illegal operation per gang, a stealth jewelry job, and the list's oddball world moments. Robberies are required in full by the 100% checklist and generate the Marked Bills that stage 6 launders.

stages.name: Money and property
stages.rationale: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills, spend $100,000 across shops, buy all eight garages and register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. These complete themselves if you launder after every robbery and buy property as areas open.

stages.name: 100% completion — A Long Road
stages.rationale: After the credits, work the checklist at Progress > Stats > 100% Completion: it is roughly 60% true completion, needs the fully-required categories plus 70 of 80 challenges and 100 optional missions, and nothing on it is missable.

stages.name: The platinum — Vice Got a Price!
stages.rationale: With every other trophy earned — the story set, the strands, the counters, the activities and A Long Road — the platinum pops on its own; there is nothing extra to do. If it does not pop, one cleanup trophy is still missing: compare your earned list against the checklist.

missables.note: The full list was screened trophy by trophy against the official descriptions and the published guides (PowerPyx, GTABase, KeenGamer and GTA-Zone). Exactly one trophy is flagged — as a potential missable, below. No mission replay exists, but free roam continues after the story and every quest giver returns, so nothing else can be permanently missed.

items.name: Positive Mental Attitude
items.when: Locks when Chapter 1 ends: the Chapter 1 balcony meditation at Jason’s house becomes unavailable once Chapter 1 ends. In Chapter 1, after the mission Down to Earth, Lucia announces a morning meditation at Jason’s house and goes to the balcony; follow her and accept before finishing the chapter.
items.detail: Why “potential”: the balcony meditation raises the meditation counter but is not marked as one of the 18 spots, so whether the trophy strictly requires it is unresolved in every published guide. The decision rule used here: if the balcony is one of the 18 marked spots, the trophy is missable; if it is not, it stays earnable in free roam. Since no source resolves it, the trophy is flagged as the safe default and the meditation is worth the two minutes. The 100% checklist separately needs only 15 of the 18 marked spots, so A Long Road is never at risk from this.
items.label: Potential missable

alsoGoodToKnow: There is no mission replay and no New Game+, so keep a manual save at the start and end of each chapter (15 manual slots are available) and rotate the spares.
Cheats disable trophies and saving — keep them off for the whole trophy run; they only unlock after the credits anyway.
Several optional missions and quest givers disappear or pause during the story, but the guides confirm none of them gate a trophy: every trophy quest giver returns, including after the story.
The 'Irredeemable' criminal profile is permanent once earned and makes police more aggressive, but the guides confirm it does not block any trophy.

cleared.name: Actions Speak Louder
cleared.line: PlayStation tracks it as a cumulative counter to 500 choices, so no single choice can lock it — it fills up as you play.
